 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Los Angeles Lakers have all the makings of a title contender.
 The Lakers are tied with the San Antonio Spurs for the best record in the NBA at 12-2. Los Angeles is cruising, playing inspired team basketball; however, the focal point of it all is Luka Doncic .
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Doncic is having the best start of his NBA career, and it's probably not even close. The Lakers superstar is dominating in all facets of the game (yes, even on defense). Doncic is playing out of his mind, and because of that, the Lakers are surprising a ton of skeptics with their stellar play thus far.
 While there are still doubters, it's tough to dismiss the Lakers as legitimate contenders as things stand.
 Doncic is playing like the MVP of the league, so much so that he is receiving MVP chants on the road. That was the case on Sunday in Phoenix.
 Doncic received MVP chants in the closing moments of the game after the Lakers weathered the Suns' fourth-quarter comeback attempt.
 Collin Sexton Explains Why Fans Are Flocking to Watch Luka Doncic
 The Lakers, including Collin Sexton, took notice.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Sexton loved what he heard down the stretch of that contest.
 "He's been playing his [bleep] off," Sexton said.
 "Everyone is coming to the game to watch him put on a show. ... At the end of the day, we all want to see him win MVP. I know I do."
 Doncic admitted he couldn't help but smile at the MVP chants he received.
 "It was very nice. I think everybody can see my smile at the free-throw line. And so, that made me happy, honestly," Doncic said.
 Luka Doncic is Making an Early Statement in NBA MVP Race
 If the season ended today, Doncic would likely be the MVP of the season.
 Through 12 games this season, Doncic is averaging 39.0 points (leading the league by a little under 9 points), along with 7.2 rebounds, 7.8 assists and 1.9 steals per game while shooting 48.6% from the field and 40.6% from three.
 Doncic is also averaging a career-high in player efficiency rating; he's leading the NBA's most efficient offense, and he's on track to become only the third player in the 3-point era to post a usage rate above 40.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement The six-time All-Star is also tied for second in charges drawn (four) and tied for third in defensive loose balls recovered (eight) this season.
 The Lakers have outscored opponents by 115 points with Doncic on the court during that stretch.
